problem: PointGoal navigation policies trained in simulation transfer poorly to the real world because of the sim-real visual gap. Real-robot evaluation is also slow, costly and fragile, and no study has systematically examined fusing multiple mid-level representations for sim-to-real transfer.
motivation: Mid-level representations (surface normals, keypoints3D, curvature, depth) are more domain-invariant than RGB and could remove the need for domain adaptation. Different representations may help in different situations, so adaptive fusion could improve transfer. Cheap, realistic evaluation is also needed to iterate on many models without deploying each on a robot.
key_idea: Train RL PointGoal policies in simulation on Taskonomy mid-level representations combined by early, mid or late fusion (with attention), and evaluate them cheaply by replacing simulated observations with the nearest real SfM image at the agent's pose.
insight: Multiple mid-level representations let a sim-only policy approach the performance of models adapted with real or CycleGAN images. Fusion architecture matters: late fusion improves monotonically with more representations (SPL 0.5561 with 4), while simple, max-pool SE and mid-fusion models are non-monotonic in the number of inputs. Some combinations hurt (e.g. n+d, likely from redundant geometry). The evaluation tool correlates moderately with real-world SPL (Pearson 0.5164), and policies trained on Gibson scenes generalize poorly to the office (SPL 0.0654 with 1 scene, 0.2786 with 72).
method: Evaluation tool: builds on Habitat and two aligned 3D models of the same office, a Matterport mesh for simulation and a COLMAP SfM model of ~32k real images. At each step the sim observation is replaced by the nearest real image, filtered by heading (cosine similarity 0.96) and then position, using FAISS retrieval.
Model alignment: COLMAP model_aligner registers 6k images sampled from the virtual mesh to align the SfM model's coordinate system with the mesh.
Mid-level extraction: four Taskonomy encoders (surface normals, keypoints3D, curvature, depth) map 256x256 RGB to 8x16x16 tensors.
Early-fusion encoders: 'Simple' (2 conv layers with GroupNorm, inputs stacked) and Squeeze-and-Excitation variants with channel attention after each conv (avg-pool or max-pool).
Mid-fusion: one Simple-style encoder branch per representation, with branch outputs concatenated.
Late-fusion: independent per-representation navigation models are frozen, and a policy fusion module outputs weights w so that y = A^T w over the models' action distributions.

Controller and training: 2-layer LSTM actor-critic with previous action and goal embeddings (576-d input), trained with DD-PPO for 5M frames on 100k episodes; the number of representations is grown greedily.

setting.backbone: Taskonomy mid-level encoders (frozen) + small conv fusion encoders + 2-layer LSTM actor-critic (trained from scratch); baselines use SE-ResNeXt50 pretrained with DD-PPO
setting.training_data: 100k virtual PointGoal episodes in one synthetic office (Matterport scan), 5M frames per model, DD-PPO RL; baselines fine-tuned on ~25k real images or CycleGAN-translated images
setting.observation: monocular RGB converted to mid-level representations, plus goal coordinates and previous action
setting.action_space: discrete low-level: forward 0.25 m, turn left 10°, turn right 10°, STOP
setting.simulator: Habitat (Matterport scan of an office ~150 m²); evaluation via the SfM real-image replacement tool
setting.privileged: none at test time (the evaluation tool uses real-image poses only for evaluation); GPS+compass-style goal coordinates are given

numbers.eval_set_note: 1000 episodes in one office, real-image substitution; success within 0.20 m, 200 step budget
numbers.extra: trained only in simulation, no domain adaptation
trained on Gibson 72 scenes, tested on unseen office
numbers.evidence: Late-fusion-72 model achieved a higher SPL value of 0.2786

numbers_note: Real-robot results (six trajectories x 3 runs) are given only in figures, except in-text SPLs: mean 0.7103 for the proposed models; Simple 1 rep 0.6906; Simple 2 reps 0.8029; SE avg 2 reps 0.7581; SE max 4 reps 0.7385; Mid-fusion 4 reps 0.7603; Late-fusion 4 reps 0.7497. The benchmark is a custom office environment, not a standard benchmark.
results: In the realistic-episode evaluation, the best mid-level models (Late-fusion 4 reps SPL 0.5561 / SR 0.7110; SE avg-pool 4 reps SPL 0.5440) far exceed RGB Synthetic (0.2610 / 0.3990) but stay below RGB Synthetic + CycleGAN (0.5985 / 0.7500) and RGB Synthetic + Real (0.8269 / 0.9640). On the real robot nearly all models reached the goals, with SPLs around 0.70–0.80 that match or beat the adapted baselines. The tool's SPL correlates with real SPL at Pearson 0.5164, with over 70% of estimates within 0.1 SPL.
limitations: Single office environment; generalization to unseen environments is poor (SPL 0.0654 with 1 Gibson scene, 0.2786 with 72), so training on the target environment's synthetic model is needed.

Real-world test has only six trajectories x 3 runs with an accurate-actuator robot and no noise study. The tool-to-real correlation is moderate (0.52), and the tool needs an extensive SfM image set of the target space.
builds_on: Sax et al. mid-level visual priors
